summary: Technically sound and weekend-buildable, but demand rests on questionnaire text and vendor blogs with no buyer who lost a deal. Free OSS tools are the real competitor, and it's unproven that a vendor-run report satisfies a reviewer.

demand.evidence: Only questionnaire templates and vendor blogs; RESEARCH.md found no first-person account of a lost deal; $16K+ prices are vendor self-reported.

statusQuo.evidence: Reassurance prose, system-prompt guards or a weekend with free promptfoo/garak/PyRIT; cheap and good enough until a reviewer pushes back.

specificity.evidence: Founder/CTO of a 3-50 person agent startup with a deal stuck in security review; no named person, buyer (seller vs enterprise) ambiguous.

wedge.evidence: Four canary-detected trap classes plus a replayable report is shippable in a weekend, but paid trust for an unknown solo author is unproven.

futureFit.evidence: More tool-using agents raise demand for dated per-model evidence, but market consolidation and bundling by labs and suites thin the moat.

premises: Agent startups face security reviews asking for injection-test evidence (supported by questionnaires, no buyer stories)
Startups pay $299-$999 instead of running promptfoo (unsupported)
Reviewers accept a vendor-run self-test report (unsupported)
Testing the real tool environment beats model-level probes (plausible)
An unknown solo author can sell security assurance (weak)
alternatives: Minimal: open-source M1 plus a sample report, posted to agent-builder communities
Ideal: hosted gauntlet with score cards, CI diff and Stripe checkout
Lateral: contribute traps as a promptfoo plugin or AgentDojo-style pack for reputation
No David repo to extend; dawnlog's run-receipt format could be reused for logs
wedge: A public sample report for a vulnerable stub agent plus a 4-trap local range; the test is whether builders ask for a run on their real agent.

feasibility.notes: Fastify/Node, two stub agents, scorer, static HTML/JSON report. Proof test: vulnerable stub 4/4 fell, hardened stub 0/4, byte-identical report JSON on re-run. Proves the code, not demand.

risks: Demand inferred from questionnaires, no buyer behavior
Free OSS substitutes and promptfoo going to OpenAI
Liability if a clean report precedes an incident
Trust in an unknown solo security author
killCriteria: Drop if, after about 15 contacts, fewer than 2 of 5 say a sample report would help a real security review, if no one shares a real questionnaire, if fewer than 20 agents run the free gauntlet in a month, or if nobody pays $299 within 60 days.
